articles.title: The Real Legacy Of Gloria Steinem
articles.author: Carrie Gress
articles.summary: Glowing obituaries are pouring in after the death of feminist icon Gloria Steinem, who was born in 1934. The Associated Press called her “a potent voice of US feminism,” and the Washington Post heralded her as the “lodestar of the modern women’s movement.” It is hard to overstate her influence upon Western women. Gloria Steinem wasn’t just one among many feminists; she was the “it” girl who normalized feminism and made it broadly attractive. And then came Gloria. Her long blond tresses, aviator glasses, and lithe physique opened the door to a new chapter for feminism. She was articulate, savvy, and a fresh force for the feminist movement. Not everyone appreciated the star power she brought to the movement. stories.summary: Markets rallied and global bond yields dipped Thursday after a US Federal Reserve governor advocated holding interest rates steady if inflation continues to cool. “ Give disinflation a chance ,” Christopher Waller said, citing “slow but continued progress” toward the Fed’s goal of 2% inflation. The market odds of a September hike fell to 50% days after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s hawkish Jackson Hole speech prompted traders to price in a rate increase . Both Waller and the New York Fed President John Williams suggested tariffs and war-related energy spikes’ inflationary effects were temporary and fading, but “ there’s no clear signs right now ” whether existing policy will bring inflation down to target, Williams said. — Brendan Ruberry
